title: Create unified ability parser in universal/
description:
Multiple parsers independently parse abilities from HTML: creatures (process_interaction_ability), monster families (parse_ability_nodes in change_extraction.py), monster templates (same), and feats/skills also need it. Each implementation handles addons, traits, actions, and afflictions differently (or not at all — the family parser doesn't handle any of them properly). Create a single universal_parse_abilities() function in universal/ that: 1. Takes raw BeautifulSoup nodes (NOT pre-processed text) 2. Splits on /
boundaries to identify ability entries 3. Extracts name + optional link from or tags 4. Extracts action_type from elements 5. Extracts traits from parenthesized text at description start 6. Merges addon fields (Requirements, Effect, Trigger, Frequency, Cost, Duration, Critical Success/Failure, etc.) into preceding ability 7. Detects affliction patterns (Saving Throw + Stage N) and restructures as affliction objects All parsers (creatures, monster families, monster templates, feats, skills) should call this instead of their own implementations. The content filters should NOT unwrap action spans — the unified parser needs them intact. Prerequisite: stop unwrapping action spans in monster_family._content_filter and monster_template._content_filter.
notes: Analysis complete. 7 parsers with 5 different action type implementations, 3 trait approaches, 3 addon/bold field approaches. Only creatures handle afflictions. Key shared functions already exist: extract_action_type (action.py), extract_starting_traits (trait.py), extract_bold_fields (universal.py). The unified parser needs to combine all of these and add affliction detection. Parsers to update: creatures, monster_families, monster_templates, feats, skills.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete in PR #94. universal/ability.py created, monster families (191/191) and templates (55/55) migrated. Creature and feat/skill migration tracked separately in PFSRD2-Parser-ob6w and PFSRD2-Parser-91hd.

title: Repeated addon label silently overwrites: 13 files lose published text
description:
universal/ability.py:_apply_addon ends in `ability[key] = value`. If a label appears twice on one ability the second value silently overwrites the first, and the earlier published text exists nowhere in the output. No error, valid schema. Adding the one-line guard assert key not in ability, ( f"{ability.get('name')!r} publishes {addon_name!r} twice; the second " f"value would overwrite {ability[key]!r}" ) surfaces 13 files with real, ALREADY-SHIPPED loss. It was written and validated during PR #165, then removed from that PR because 13 failing files violates the zero-errors policy and the fixes are a separate concern from that PR's subject. The guard should land together with the fixes below. FAILING FILES (13) MonsterFamilies.aspx.ID_396 'Repelling Blast' publishes 'Effect' twice MonsterFamilies.aspx.ID_585 'Afterimage Jumps' publishes 'Frequency' twice Hazards.aspx.ID_45, 48, 282, 351, 382, 393, 458, 487, 488, 568, 609 None are caused by PR #165. The two family cases are Effect/Frequency, which were already in DEFAULT_ADDON_LABELS before that PR; hazards already had the degree labels. A full creature run (3670 files) fires the assert ZERO times, so creatures are clean. DIAGNOSED EXAMPLE — Hazards ID_45 (gm_core/confounding_betrayal) Bold sequence in the source: Unmask ... Trigger ... Critical Success ... Success ... Critical Failure ... Routine ... Critical Success ... Success ... Critical Failure ... There are two degree runs. The first belongs to the Unmask reaction; the second belongs to the Routine's save. `Routine` is a hazard FIELD_LABEL, extracted separately rather than starting a new ability, so the Unmask ability is still open when the second run arrives and swallows it. Shipped result in hazards/gm_core/confounding_betrayal.json: Unmask carries the SECOND critical_success ("The creature is unaffected and temporarily immune for 1 minute."), and the first ("The creature sees through the illusions entirely and is temporarily immune to the haunt's routine for 1 minute.") appears nowhere in the file. So the real hazard defect is that a degree run following a field label is attributed to the previous ability. Fixing that probably fixes most or all of the 11 hazard cases; the 2 family cases need their own look (likely missing
in the source, i.e. HTML bugs). WORK 1. investigate each of the 13: HTML bug (fix pfsrd2-web) vs parser bug (fix code) 2. land the assert once they parse clean 3. re-run hazards and families and review the recovered text in the data diff Found by strategic-fragility-reviewer on PR #165, comment 3790798599.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #167 (squash-merged). _set_once guards the repeated addon label; hazard routine degrees became structured routine_results; 3 HTML fixes in pfsrd2-web (ID_297, ID_601, plus ability-name bolds). 606 hazards / 0 errors, 1722 tests.

title: Composite item references: address '+1 striking shock longsword' as a thing
description:
THE KEYSTONE PROBLEM. A composite item — a base item plus potency plus fundamental and property runes, optionally of a precious material — has no identity anywhere in the data. It is not a document, has no game-id, and cannot be linked to. Consumers can only see the name string.

What exists today, in stat_block.gear (1856 creatures, 5433 entries):

- 4747 entries carry links, so the PARTS are often addressable: '+1 striking longsword' resolves to striking (Equipment 280) and longsword (Weapons 31).
- 1181 entries begin with a potency bonus and the potency is NEVER linked. The '+1' lives only in the name string, even though Weapon Potency and Armor Potency are real documents with per-grade variants.
- AoN's own link granularity is inconsistent: the same concept appears as 'striking', '1 striking' and '+1 striking' across entries.
- 1107 rune-bearing entries do already have a resolved base item, so the raw material is better than it looks.

The consequence: nothing can answer 'what does this creature's weapon actually do'. The rune effects work (PFSRD2-Parser-dsx1) can compute what a shock rune adds, but there is no addressable thing to add it TO.

This is also why specific magic items are stuck — see the sibling ticket on weapon facts.
design:
A composite is a RECIPE over addressable parts, not a document to synthesise. Combinatorially there are millions; do not generate them.

Proposed shape on a gear entry, beside the existing name and links rather than replacing them:

  item_reference: {
    base: { game-id, game-obj, name },      # longsword
    potency: 1,                              # from the name string; Weapon Potency variant is addressable
    fundamental: [ { game-id, name, grade } ],   # striking / greater striking
    property: [ { game-id, name } ],             # shock, flaming
    material: { game-id, name } | null,          # cold iron, mithral
    quantity: 1
  }

Parse from the name string, validate against the existing links rather than trusting either alone — the links are the ground truth for identity, the name string is the ground truth for potency and ordering. Where they disagree, that is a source or parser bug worth surfacing, not silently reconciling.

Never invent a part that is not in the name. An unparseable gear string keeps its name and gets needs_review.
acceptance_criteria: A consumer can take a creature's gear entry and resolve every component to a game-id, including the potency grade; the 1181 potency-bearing entries carry a numeric potency; disagreements between name and links are reported rather than guessed; unparseable entries are flagged not fabricated.

title: Executable item effects: make runes change the item they are etched on
description:
Today only 22 fundamental/reinforcing rune grades carry executable effects (46 effect objects across 13 documents). All 141 property runes ship prose only, so a +1 striking shock longsword does not add its 1d6 electricity anywhere a consumer can read it.

The survey behind this epic (2026-08-15) found the property runes are not one problem but four, with very different costs:

1. UNCONDITIONAL ON-HIT DAMAGE — 18 documents (~10 runes x 2 editions): Shock, Flaming, Frost, Corrosive, Thundering, Astral, Brilliant, Decaying, Disrupting, Impactful, Nightmare, Unholy. Text is highly regular ('deals an additional 1d6 fire damage on a successful Strike'). Needs no new schema: append an attack_damage entry, a shape that already ships on creatures.

2. CONDITIONAL EFFECTS — the vocabulary gap. Bane and Giant-Killing are creature-type gated; Energy-Resistant grants a resistance the CRAFTER CHOOSES; crit riders fire only on a critical hit. All three need a condition qualifier on the effect, and the crafter-choice case needs the engine's existing but unused 'select' operation.

3. ACTIVATED ABILITIES — 17 property runes mention activation and ZERO of 141 carry any structured activation data. Activation is generally an action, so the honest model is that the item grants an action: the same ability shape with an action_type that creatures already use. This is wider than runes — every activatable item has the same gap.

4. NOT MECHANICAL — roughly 50 weapon and 33 armor runes are rule overrides or narrative (Ghost Touch's targeting rule, Misleading's flat-check DC, Fortification's crit-to-hit conversion). These keep their prose and get needs_review. Never fabricate an effect.

Armor is the more heterogeneous half and was under-examined before this survey: 43 property runes, of which only a handful are passive numeric changes.
design:
Do tier 1 first because it needs no schema change and proves the pipeline end to end. Tier 2 is one design decision (a condition qualifier) that unlocks type-gating, crit-gating and crafter choice together — do not solve them separately. Tier 3 is a different shape entirely and should not hide inside the rune work.

Reference implementations already in the corpus: attack_damage with persistent:true ships 564 times on creatures; a damage entry with notes 'on a critical hit' ships twice; condition riders ship as modifier entries with a Conditions link; the damage types runes need (spirit 220, evil 204, good 66, holy 1) are all proven.
acceptance_criteria: A consumer can ask 'what damage does this runed weapon do' and get an answer for the tier-1 runes; tier-2 conditions are expressible without fabricating; activation is tracked separately; everything else keeps prose plus needs_review.
notes:
Children (bd cannot model epic->task membership as a dependency, so recorded here):

  j1w3  Composite item references — THE KEYSTONE. Nothing else delivers user-visible
        value without it, because there is no addressable thing to apply effects to.
  vu32  Weapon facts on specific magic weapons — 277 items have no weapon_modes,
        so eligibility and damage cannot be computed for them.
  vqjp  Tier 1: on-hit damage for the 18 unconditional runes. Blocked by j1w3 + vu32.
  ec7r  Tier 2: conditional effects (type gates, crit gates, crafter choice). Blocked by vqjp.
  bstt  Item activation as a granted action. Independent of the others; wider than runes.
  14ie  The original enrichment-sidecar ticket, now the delivery mechanism for vqjp/ec7r.

Suggested order: vu32 and j1w3 in parallel, then vqjp, then ec7r. bstt any time.

Survey date 2026-08-15, against 141 distinct property runes and 5433 creature gear entries.

title: Rune effects must use the template engine's target+operation vocabulary
description:
Rune effects ship as {operation, subject, value|modifier} with NO target. The consumer that executes effects — pfsrd2-data-api's template engine — decodes Effect{Target, Operation, ...}, has no subject field, calls resolvePath(statBlock, eff.Target) and errors when it cannot resolve. It also has no 'set' operation. So rune effects are not executable by the only engine that exists for this dataset.

I chose 'subject' deliberately, reasoning that JSONPath targets were speculative because no canonical composed item+rune document exists. That reasoning does not survive contact with the consumer: the engine's whole model is target+operation against a stat_block document, an item IS such a document, and applyAddModifier even creates the target array when it is missing.

Nothing is broken today — the only apply endpoint is creature-only — so this is latent. But a second effect vocabulary is exactly the accidental complexity to remove before anything is built on it.

Scope: 13 files, 60 effect objects (the fundamental and reinforcing grades). Materials and spell slots carry no effects at all.
design:
Map each rune effect onto an operation the engine already implements:
  weapon potency -> add_modifier @ $.stat_block.offense.weapon_modes[*].modifiers
  armor potency  -> add_modifier @ $.stat_block.defense.modifiers
  resilient      -> add_modifier @ $.stat_block.defense.modifiers
  striking       -> replace @ $.stat_block.offense.weapon_modes[*].damage[*].dice_count
  reinforcing    -> adjustment @ $.stat_block.defense.hitpoints.{hardness,hp,break_threshold}

adjustment adds a delta and syncs the sibling display text, which is exactly the reinforcing wording. replace sets a value and syncs text. Shields already expose defense.hitpoints.{hardness,hp,break_threshold} so those targets resolve today.

Striking needs dice_count, which weapon damage does not currently expose (only formula: '1d8'). Structuring that is a prerequisite and is worth doing on its own merits per the project mission.

property_rune_slots is capacity metadata rather than a mutation and moves out of effects onto the rune block as grants_property_slots.
acceptance_criteria: No rune effect carries 'subject'; every effect has a target that resolves against at least one real host item, enforced by pf2_verify_runes; operations are drawn only from the engine's vocabulary; weapon damage exposes dice_count and die_size; equipment parser 0 errors.
close_reason: Fixed. Rune effects now use target + operations the template engine implements (add_modifier / replace / adjustment); no effect carries subject. Weapon damage gained dice_count and die_size so striking's target resolves. Capacity moved to rune.grants_property_slots since it mutates nothing. pf2_verify_runes checks every effect target resolves, mutation-verified. Full equipment run 0 errors, all four verifiers green.

title: Staff spell lists silently dropped for 24 of 90 staves
description:
24 of 90 staves parse with variants: [] and no spell list at all, while their source HTML plainly carries one.

Verified cases:
  - Staff of Illumination (aonid 3043): HTML lists 'Cantrip light / 2nd everlight / 3rd everlight, holy light'; JSON has no variants, no rank list, no spell links.
  - Hell Staff (aonid 2253): HTML lists 9 entries across Cantrip-4th (divine lance, protection, summon lesser servitor, darkvision, chilling darkness, divine wrath); JSON has empty variants and only an incidental spell link from flavour text.

The 66 staves that DO parse present their list as markdown bullets inside variant text ('* Cantrip tanglefoot', '* 1st shocking grasp, spider sting'), with higher grades adding ranks cumulatively. The 24 that fail present it inside an 'Activate [action] Cast a Spell; Effect' block with rank-labelled lines and no variant structure — a second layout the parser does not handle.

This is the same class as the legacy Dragonhide stat-table loss fixed in PR #152: content published by AoN, absent from output, with nothing failing. Full list of affected aonids obtainable by re-running the survey in the issue notes.

Fix before any spell-slot decoration work, since that work would otherwise be built on a corpus missing a quarter of its staff spell lists.
design: Two candidate approaches: (a) teach the staff path to read the Activate/Cast-a-Spell effect block as a spell list when no variant bullets exist, or (b) find why these items produce no variants at all — empty variants plus a populated HTML block suggests the variant splitter bails before reaching the effect block. Investigate (b) first; the missing variants may be the actual root cause and the spell list a downstream symptom.
acceptance_criteria: All 90 staves expose their published spell list; a staff whose HTML advertises a Cast-a-Spell rank list but yields none fails the parse rather than shipping empty.
close_reason: Invalid — my survey was wrong. I searched only stat_block.text and variants[].text; staves without grade variants carry their spell list in stat_block.statistics.abilities[].effect, with spell links attached. Verified across the whole document: 88 of 90 staves have a structured rank list, Whispering Staff correctly has none (it functions as a major staff of the unblinking eye, delegating to another item), and Staff of the Black Desert has its list as an undelimited run-on string rather than bullets. No spell content is lost. The run-on formatting variance is real but minor and is folded into the spell-slot work instead.

title: Move creature_types list to enrichment DB table, populated by creature parser

Replace hardcoded _CREATURE_TYPES set in enrichment/change_extractor.py with a DB-backed lookup. The current set is incomplete (misses Vampire, Skeleton, ancestries, elements, Unholy, Aquatic, etc.) which caused the trait-routing fix from a10f0f4 to drop real creature_types entries to $.traits-only.

Design:
1. New creature_types table in enrichment DB (name UNIQUE).
2. Seed script reads existing pfsrd2-data/monsters to populate.
3. Creature parser adds pass to upsert creature_types it encounters (idempotent).
4. _trait_target in change_extractor.py queries DB (cached per-run).
5. Bump ENRICHMENT_VERSION.

title: Fix template 'abilities' change effects: route per-ability instead of all→defense.automatic_abilities
description: _build_effects in enrichment/change_extractor.py hardcodes a single effect targeting $.defense.automatic_abilities for category='abilities'. This causes offensive abilities added by templates (e.g., Amphibious → Drag Along, a one-action offensive ability) to be placed under defense.automatic_abilities alongside genuinely automatic abilities like Low-light Vision. Fix: emit one effect per ability, using each ability's deterministic action-type-based category (reaction→reactive, 1-2-3 action→offensive, free+trigger→reactive) with DB lookup fallback via ability_placement.lookup_ability_category, and filter source JSONPath by ability name.

title: Cache LLM responses to survive enrichment DB rebuilds
description: When the enrichment DB is deleted and rebuilt, all LLM enrichment work is lost and must be re-run (~75 min for damage alone). Design: add an llm_response_cache table keyed on (identity_hash, prompt_version) that stores the raw LLM response. When enriching, check the cache first — if the hash and prompt version match, use the cached response instead of calling the LLM. This table should either: (a) live in a separate DB file that doesn't get deleted, or (b) be resilient to the main enrichment DB being rebuilt by auto-populating from the cache on first access. The cache makes it safe to delete enrichment.db without losing expensive LLM work.

title: Monster family sections tree should remain unmodified by consolidation
description: The _consolidate_creation_changes function removes ability sections from the sections tree when moving them to subtypes. This means the raw sections tree no longer represents the original document structure. For rendering, we need the sections tree to be a faithful representation of the original HTML — changes/subtypes are enrichment overlays, not replacements for sections. Fix: stop removing sections from the tree during consolidation. The subtypes can reference sections by name or path instead of consuming them.
close_reason:
Already fixed — verified against shipped data rather than closed on the code comment alone. The ticket asked for _consolidate_creation_changes to stop removing ability sections from the sections tree, so subtypes become enrichment overlays rather than replacements. monster_family.py now says exactly that at the consolidation site ("Sections are NOT removed — they stay intact for display") and builds each subtype with a JSONPath reference to the section instead of consuming it. VERIFIED IN OUTPUT, not just in code: 632 family files, 153 of them carry subtypes. 153 of 153 subtype names are still present in their file's sections tree. The single apparent miss was dragon_time's 'Young Time Dragon"'. That is not a consolidation failure — the section is present under exactly that name, stray double-quote and all. The quote comes from the source heading

Young Time Dragon"

, and is fixed in pfsrd2-web 5ff060dd3f. Separately pinned by tests/test_ability_continuations.py::TestMonsterFamilyKeepsItsSectionText, added in PR #169: it drives _extract_section_abilities over the shape the ability parser leaves unclaimed and fails if monster_family ever reassigns or consumes section["text"] again. Adding `section["text"] = ""` to that function fails it. Closed rather than left open because the fix predates this session and the ticket's own acceptance is met; the test now guards against regression.

title: Rework activate: activations array vs polymorphic ability extension
description:
The activate pattern is becoming sticky and a poor fit for ability - like affliction, it's a superset of ability rather than fitting cleanly into it.

Two approaches to consider:

1. **Activations array approach**: Create an `activations` array containing `activate` objects. Each activate object can hold an `ability` plus have the `activation` field on it. This separates concerns cleanly.

2. **Polymorphic extension approach**: If JSON Schema supports any kind of polymorphism (oneOf, allOf, discriminator patterns), consider extending the `ability` object to become an `activation` object - essentially making activation a specialized subtype of ability.

Research needed:
- Review JSON Schema polymorphism options (oneOf with discriminator, allOf for inheritance-like patterns)
- Examine how affliction currently handles being a superset of ability
- Determine which approach better fits the existing schema patterns and parser architecture

This affects equipment.py parsing and pfsrd2/schema/equipment.schema.json.

title: Skill check needs its own object type; secondary DCs in degree text are unstructured
description:
Degree-of-success text names DCs that are NOT saving throws, and nothing captures any of them structurally.

DEVON'S DESIGN CALL: a skill check probably wants a new object type, mostly the same as save_dc, called something like skill_check, carrying the skill (e.g. Acrobatics).

MEASURED — 20 secondary DCs inside degree fields across hazards/families/templates:

   10  bare "DC 25"      the check type appears later in the sentence, not adjacent to the DC
    5  save              "DC 33 Reflex save to avoid", "DC 32 basic Reflex save"
    2  skill check       "DC 30 Acrobatics check"          <- needs the new type
    2  flat check        "DC 5 flat check or they..."
    1  "DC 45 checks to Escape from"

Examples:
   test_of_agility        Tilt and Roll     success           "DC 30 Acrobatics check"
   test_of_agility        Tilt and Roll     failure           "DC 33 Reflex save"
   disorienting_illusions Disorient         critical_failure  "DC 5 flat check"
   the_putrid_rise        Vomit             critical_failure  "DC 32 basic Reflex save"
   collapsing_cell        Collapse          failure           "DC 25"  (type stated later in the sentence)

So three shapes are in play, and they are genuinely different things:
   - saving throw  -> existing save_dc, save_type Fort/Ref/Will
   - flat check    -> existing save_dc convention (a flat check occupies the same slot as Will/Fort — Devon, see tys6)
   - skill check   -> NEW object type, same shape as save_dc plus the skill name

The bare "DC 25" majority is the hard part: the DC and the check type are separated by prose, so a naive regex on the DC will not tell you which of the three it is. Whatever is built needs to fail loudly rather than guess — misclassifying a skill check as a save produces plausible-looking wrong data.

These are SECONDARY checks described inside an outcome, not the ability's own save, so they must not be merged into ability["saving_throw"]. Cloud of Ashes' own save is DC 30 Fort and is correct; its failure text separately names a DC 5 flat check.

NOT a regression from PR #167 — verified that zero of these were structured before that change either.

title: Model flat checks as a boolean on save_dc, not as save_type
description:
A flat check is a d20 rolled with no bonuses — it describes the TYPE OF ROLL, not a saving throw. Modelling it as save_type="Flat Check" conflates a roll type with the Fort/Ref/Will axis.

DEVON'S DECISION: a boolean on save_dc that can be set to true is an acceptable answer.

    {"dc": 5, "flat_check": true, "subtype": "save_dc", "text": "DC 5 flat check"}

rather than

    {"dc": 5, "save_type": "Flat Check", ...}

SCOPE (measured against shipped data)

  save_dc objects currently carrying save_type="Flat Check":
      monsters            212 objects / 167 files
      npcs                 43 objects /  40 files
      monster_families     13 objects /  10 files
      monster_templates     1 object  /   1 file
      TOTAL               269 objects / 218 files

  The mapping lives in universal/creatures.py (~line 300): "flat" -> "Flat Check".

WORK
 1. add `flat_check` (boolean) to the save_dc definition, copied byte-identically into every schema that defines save_dc (creature, hazard, affliction, spell, equipment... check docs/schema-guide.md for the full list)
 2. stop emitting save_type="Flat Check"; set flat_check=true instead
 3. decide whether save_type should be absent or retained when flat_check is true — a flat check has no save axis, so absent is probably right
 4. full re-run of every affected content type; this touches 218 files of shipped data
 5. tell the pfsrd2-data-api / pfsrd2-automation consumers: docs/affliction-data-consumer-guide.md and docs/hazard-data-consumer-guide.md both document save_dc

SEPARATE BUT RELATED (do not conflate)
17 abilities name a DC ONLY inside degree-of-success text ("must succeed at a DC 5 flat check", "DC 30 Acrobatics", "DC 32 basic") and NONE of them capture it structurally. That is a secondary check described within an outcome — it is not the ability's own save, so it must not be merged into the ability's saving_throw. It needs its own home. Long-standing gap, not introduced by PR #167.

Found while reviewing the monster_family diff on PR #167: dragon_cinder's Cloud of Ashes keeps its real save (DC 30 Fort); what disappeared was a save_dc hanging off a BOGUS "Failure" ability, carrying save_type="Flat Check". Nothing correct was lost — but the DC in that sentence is real data and is now unstructured.
close_reason:
Resolved by Devon in discussion: a flat check occupies the same slot as a Will or Fort save — it is the kind of check being rolled. So save_type='Flat Check' is already the right shape, and the 269 save_dc objects across 218 files need no migration.

The boolean alternative was floated and then withdrawn in favour of this simpler reading. No code or schema change required.

What remains real is the SEPARATE gap, tracked on PFSRD2-Parser-mgz4: 17 abilities name a DC only inside degree-of-success text ('must succeed at a DC 5 flat check', 'DC 30 Acrobatics', 'DC 32 basic') and none capture it structurally. That is a secondary check described within an outcome, so it must not be merged into the ability's own saving_throw.

title: Ability names and Melee labels published without <b> misparse silently
description: An ability name or attack label published without its tags sits as plain text inside the previous ability's effect. The name is lost, its traits and action type are lost, and its addon fields are attributed to the wrong ability. PR #167 fixed three of these, but only because they happened to COLLIDE and trip the repeated-label guard (Scything Wings, Dematerialize, Violent Deluge). The rest misparse silently and nothing fires. DETECTOR (found by code-reviewer on #167, reproduced and widened): an action span whose immediately preceding markup is not or python - <<'PY' import re,os,glob web=os.environ["PF2_WEB_DIR"] pat=re.compile(r'([^>]{0,60}?)\s*") or before.endswith("") or not before: continue words=re.sub("<[^>]*>","",before).strip() if words and not words.endswith((";",":",",")): print(os.path.basename(f), "...", " ".join(words.split()[-4:])) PY CURRENT HITS (9; two are likely false positives worth confirming) Hazards ID_575 Scythe Shuffle — ability referenced by name 3x elsewhere while the ability itself is a text blob Hazards ID_528, 595, 338, 354, 554 Melee — the whole attack line sits in `text` instead of parsing as an attack MonsterFamilies ID_585 Second Glance — buried in Afterimage Jumps' effect, traits lost. NOTE: this is the same file PR #167 already fixed for Dematerialize Hazards ID_245 "...a cracked-open door, or" — probably a legitimate mid-prose action span, check MonsterFamilies ID_587 "...)" — probably legitimate, check ALSO, same class, degree-shaped: Hazards ID_581 Critical Effect typo (should be Critical Failure) -> becomes a bogus ability, and the routine loses its critical failure APPROACH Root CLAUDE.md: a one-off is fixed in the HTML, a consistent pattern is solved in code. Three was a one-off; ten is a pattern — but a parser heuristic for "unbolded ability name in prose" is guesswork, and the code-reviewer on #167 argued (persuasively) that per-file HTML fixes remain the right call. The detector above is the thing to keep: run it as a check so new instances surface instead of silently misparsing. Fix the HTML, then re-run hazards/families and review the recovered abilities and attacks in the diff. Found by code-reviewer and strategic-fragility-reviewer on PR #167 (comments 3791300815, 3791381961).

title: Concurrent parser runs race on the enrichment DB (UNIQUE constraint on ability_records)
description:
Two parser runs against the same enrichment DB can collide and fail a file.

Observed during PR #165 review, when a reviewer agent and the main session were both running parsers:

  MonsterFamilies.aspx.ID_585
  sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: ability_records.identity_hash
  at pfsrd2/sql/enrichment/queries.py:24

Re-parsed on its own, the same file passes. So it is a fetch-then-insert race in the shared enrichment DB (~/.pfsrd2/pfsrd2.db), not a data or parser defect.

Why it matters now: the pr-review-loop spawns reviewer agents that verify claims by running the parsers themselves, so concurrent runs are no longer rare — they are the normal case during a review. A spurious failure in that window looks exactly like a real regression and costs a full investigation to dismiss.

Options, roughly in order of appeal:
 1. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING / INSERT OR IGNORE at that insert site, since the identity_hash is the dedup key anyway
 2. wrap fetch-then-insert in a transaction with a retry on IntegrityError
 3. document that parser runs must be serialised, and have reviewers work from a copy of the DB

Also worth checking whether other enrichment insert sites have the same shape.

Reported by code-reviewer on PR #165.

title: Committed monster data is stale: 6 files lose structured objects on regen
description:
Committed monster data is stale relative to what main's parser produces. Found while verifying PR #165 had no collateral damage.

A full creature run on main (or on any current branch) rewrites 6 files that differ from what is committed:

  monsters/bestiary/slurk.json
  monsters/bestiary_2/rhinoceros.json
  monsters/gatewalkers_hardcover/kareq.json
  monsters/monster_core/rhinoceros.json
  monsters/monster_core/slurk.json
  monsters/pathfinder_187_the_seventh_arch/kareq.json

In every case the regenerated file LOSES structured objects the committed file has:

  slurk       Belly Grease      saving_throw [{dc 18, save_type ...}] gone
  rhinoceros  (ability)         damage [{formula 3d8+6}] gone
  kareq       (ability)         similar

Proven not to be a regression from #165: I built a throwaway worktree at main, ran a real (non-dry) parse of Monsters.aspx.ID_4005 with both main and the PR branch, and the two outputs are byte-identical. Both produce 0 saving_throw where the committed file has 1. So main and the branch agree; the committed DATA is what disagrees.

Two possible explanations, needs investigation:
 1. the committed data was generated before some parser change and never regenerated, or
 2. ability/monster-ability DB enrichment produces different results now than when the data was committed (the run logs warnings like "_pick_best_ability: no edition match for Darkvision (target=legacy), using first of 2", so enrichment picks among DB candidates and is sensitive to DB state)

If (2), see .claude/skills/rebuild-enrichment.md — the enrichment DB may need a rebuild before the data is regenerated, and whichever direction is correct should be decided deliberately rather than by whoever runs the parser next.

Either way this is a live inconsistency: anyone doing a full creature run gets 6 unexplained changed files in their diff, which is exactly the noise that makes real regressions hard to spot.

title: Monster families/templates lose ability-block nodes the parser doesn't claim
description:
Found by strategic-fragility-reviewer during PR #165 (thread 3790710012). parse_abilities_from_nodes takes an optional consumed= set. Callers that pass it can tell which nodes the ability parser claimed and keep the rest in their own tree. Callers that do not have already had the nodes extracted by collect_ability_nodes, so anything unclaimed is silently gone. pfsrd2/hazard.py passes consumed= -> unclaimed nodes preserved pfsrd2/change_extraction.py passes consumed= -> preserved pfsrd2/monster_family.py does NOT -> unclaimed nodes LOST pfsrd2/monster_template.py does NOT -> LOST Reviewer's repro (on the PR #165 branch): Big Attack The dragon breathes.
Success Half damage.
This trailing paragraph belongs to Big Attack and lives nowhere else.
before: Big Attack; Success(text='Half damage. This trailing paragraph ...') after: Big Attack(success='Half damage.') # paragraph gone The mechanism is _split_nodes setting glue_blocked = _is_label(current[0]), which skips the continuation branch; the node then falls through to the final "if current" (False) and is dropped with no assert. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by #165: this loses ANY unclaimed node in a family/template ability block, not just continuations after a degree. Widening the addon label set in #165 adds one more route to it. Verified no family/template/hazard file hits it today (word-bag diff of all 17 changed files vs HEAD shows only the label names disappearing), so it is latent. FIX: thread consumed= through monster_family.py:531 and monster_template.py:270 and restore what the parser did not claim, mirroring hazard.py:498 and change_extraction.py:95. Expect a data diff — text that is currently vanishing should come back — so re-run families and templates and review what reappears. DO NOT fix by asserting in universal/ability.py._split_nodes: an unconsumed node is legitimate for callers that pass consumed=, and a blanket assert there fails 6 existing tests (test_hazard.py::TestAbilityLeftovers::test_prose_between_abilities_is_not_dropped and test_unified_ability.py::TestParseAbilitiesFromNodes::test_no_abilities among them). I tried exactly that first. gh api /repos/devonjones/PFSRD2-Parser/pulls/165/comments/3790710012
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-16 after #167 merged. The prescribed fix is a no-op or harmful for BOTH callers; the mechanism is real but the consequence differs by caller because of what each does with bs afterwards. METHOD: monkeypatched _extract_abilities_from_bs in-process to pass consumed= and report unclaimed nodes, then drove the REAL pipeline (parse_monster_family / parse_monster_template) over the whole corpus. 632 families and 55 templates, 0 errors. A first probe over raw HTML was invalid — it bypassed the pre-filters and picked up the Source header — so the numbers below are from the real path only. monster_template (55 files): bs IS written back. monster_template.py:233 does remaining = str(bs).strip() source_section["text"] = remaining so unclaimed nodes really would be lost here. But across all 55 templates the ONLY unclaimed nodes are bare
separators (8 sites; ID_12 has six, ID_15 five). Re-appending those would inject stray hard breaks into section text — strictly worse output. monster_family (632 files): bs is a DELIBERATE COPY. monster_family.py:497-499 says so: "Parse a COPY — collect_ability_nodes mutates the tree via extract(), but we want section text to stay intact for display." The abilities/spells are taken and bs is discarded; section["text"] is never reassigned. So unclaimed nodes are NOT lost, and appending them to that throwaway bs — which is what the FIX section prescribes — does nothing at all. 221 family sites do have unclaimed CONTENT rather than just separators. ID_145 and ID_159 leave a Related Groups field unclaimed, and ID_159 leaves the prose "If the animal succeeds at its save, the vrykolakas can attempt to possess a different animal within 100 feet...". All of it survives in shipped output: Related Groups appears in 86 family JSON files, and the vrykolakas prose is in vampire_vrykolakas.json. What is lost is only the ATTRIBUTION — that prose is not attached to the ability it continues — which is a different and smaller defect than "lost". Also verified: 66/66 family sections that carry abilities still contain every one of their ability names in section["text"]. PROPOSED REPLACEMENT FIX: thread consumed= through monster_template only, and instead of re-appending, ASSERT that the unclaimed remainder carries no published text (separators and whitespace only). That turns the one genuinely silent drop into a loud failure and changes no output today. Leave monster_family alone and document the copy, so the next reader does not "fix" a no-op. This does not touch _split_nodes, so the 6-test warning in the description still holds and is still respected. The attribution gap in families is worth its own ticket rather than being folded in here. The families attribution gap is now PFSRD2-Parser-9oge.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #169, but NOT with the fix prescribed here. Measurement first, then the fix that measurement supported. The prescription — thread consumed= through both callers and restore the unclaimed nodes — is a no-op in one file and harmful in the other: monster_family parses a COPY and never reassigns section["text"], so appending unclaimed nodes to that throwaway soup does nothing. Verified three ways across the review: 66/66 (later 291/291) family sections that carry abilities still contain every ability name in their text; "Related Groups" ships in 86 family JSON files; ID_159's continuation prose ships in vampire_vrykolakas.json. monster_template DOES write str(bs) back, so a node unclaimed there really is lost. But the only unclaimed nodes across all 55 templates are the
separators — 24 of them across 8 sites in 7 files, independently re-derived by two reviewers. Restoring them would inject stray hard breaks. WHAT LANDED: consumed= threaded through the template extractor, plus an assert that every unclaimed node is a
or whitespace. Output unchanged; the one genuinely silent drop in the file is now a loud failure. This is closer to what the original PR #165 reviewer asked for than the ticket text was — their comment ended "the ladder-consistent fix is an assert on the dropped node rather than a continue". The DO-NOT warning in the description still holds and was respected: nothing was asserted in _split_nodes. SIX review rounds, five legitimate P2s, all in the tests rather than the guard. The residue is PFSRD2-Parser-9oge (families attribution: continuation prose ships but is not attached to the ability it continues).

title: Monster family/template stat-block fields parsed as abilities
description:
Found by code-reviewer during PR #165.

Bold labels that name stat-block fields are being emitted as subtype=ability entries on monster families and templates, instead of as changes to the stat block. 47 files, 88 entries in the current corpus:

  Darkvision        32
  Immunities        23
  Resistances       11
  Low-Light Vision   9
  Fly Speed          4
  Climb Speed        4
  Weaknesses         3
  Speed              1
  Low-light Vision   1

Immunities / Resistances / Weaknesses / Climb-Fly-Swim Speed / Speed are unambiguously stat changes and do not belong in abilities[]. Darkvision and Low-Light Vision are senses — creatures model those as abilities with subtype=ability elsewhere, so those two may be correct as-is; decide deliberately rather than sweeping them together.

Note 'Low-Light Vision' and 'Low-light Vision' both appear, so whatever handles these should normalise case.

This is NOT the same as PFSRD2-Parser-alj, which was about addon labels (Trigger/Effect/Requirements and the degrees of success) splitting one ability into several. That is fixed. This is a different question: which bold labels are abilities at all.

Related: the changes/subtypes machinery already exists (pfsrd2/change_extraction.py, parse_change) and is where these likely belong.

title: feat parser silently overwrites same-named feats (Directional Bombs)
description:
Found while verifying PR #162 had no collateral data change.

feats/player_core_2/directional_bombs.json is written by TWO different Feats.aspx entries — aonid 104 and aonid 5779 — and whichever parses last wins. The committed file is aonid 5779 (level 6, archetype_level 8, with a 'different level than displayed here' note); reparsing a subset that includes aonid 104 replaces it with a level 8 feat carrying no archetype note.

This is the same silent-overwrite class as the 19 duplicated GM Core curses that PR #162 fixed, but pfsrd2/feat.py:812 write_feat still builds its path as jsondir + char_replace(name) + '.json' with no collision handling.

The fix now exists and is shared: universal.files.disambiguated_filename(jsondir, struct, label), added in #162 and already used by hazard.py and affliction.py. It compares only aonid (stable across parser changes) and gives every colliding entry an aonid suffix, so both remain addressable.

Survey of aonid-suffixed files by area (evidence of which parsers already handle this):
  feats     7708 files, 3 suffixed   <- has SOME handling, but not in write_feat
  spells    2370 files, 0 suffixed
  monsters  3670 files, 0 suffixed
  npcs       895 files, 30 suffixed
  equipment 3883 files, 2 suffixed

Worth auditing each parser's writer for the same gap, not just feat.py. Note the strategic-fragility reviewer on #162 found 51 name-pairs under monsters/+npcs/ that a naive collision glob would mishandle, which suggests monsters/npcs deserve a close look.

Out of scope for #162 (affliction parser); filed so it is not lost.
notes:
CORRECTION to the survey in the description: the 'aonid-suffixed' counts I gave were wrong. Checked the actual files — feats/rage_of_elements/hell_of_1000000_needles.json etc. are feats whose NAMES contain digits ('Hell of 1,000,000 Needles', 'Mask of The 12th Step'), not aonid suffixes. No parser was doing collision handling; the counts for npcs/equipment are suspect for the same reason and should be re-measured before being used as evidence.

What is verified: pfsrd2/feat.py had no collision handling at all (create_feat_filename was jsondir + char_replace(name) + '.json'), and the committed feat output has 2 game-id duplicates across 7708 files.
close_reason:
INVALID — I filed this on a misreading; there is no collision.

Verified by full regeneration of all 8142 feat sources with a clean output tree: 7708 files, 0 errors, and **0 changed files** versus git HEAD. The feat parser loses nothing.

The Directional Bombs pair is not a collision. They are the legacy and remastered versions of one feat, with different sources, so they write to different book directories and both already exist correctly in shipped data:
  aonid 104  legacy      Core Rulebook pg 78  -> feats/core_rulebook/directional_bombs.json
  aonid 5779 remastered  Player Core 2 pg 66  -> feats/player_core_2/directional_bombs.json

The 8142-sources vs 7708-files gap is fully accounted for and benign:
  8142 source files = 7706 clean ID_<n> + 436 ID_<n>.ArchLevel_<m> archetype-level variants
  7706 distinct aonids -> 7706 documents, +2 written to a second book dir (multi-source) = 7708
  source ids producing no output: 0

Also corrected in the notes: my original survey cited aonid-suffixed files in feats/npcs/equipment as evidence of existing collision handling. Those were feats with digits in their NAMES ('Hell of 1,000,000 Needles', 'Mask of The 12th Step'). No parser had collision handling, and none needed it.

What led me astray: I saw a git diff on feats/player_core_2/directional_bombs.json after a 50-feat subset run and attributed it to an overwrite without checking that the two entries write to different directories.

No code change shipped. If a same-book name collision ever does appear, universal.files.disambiguated_filename exists and is the house answer.

title: Affliction parser: curses and diseases
description:
Parse Curses (55 distinct) and Diseases (44) into a shared affliction shape, closing the gap PFSRD2-Parser-3xoc describes — afflictions exist today only as ability.stages on creatures and hazards, with no documents of their own.

One parser, two runs, on the equipment pattern. Output to curses/ and diseases/ with game-obj Curses and Diseases, both validating against affliction.schema.1.0.json, root key 'affliction', subtype curse|disease.

ItemCurses is deliberately NOT parsed: all 15 of its distinct entries resolve to Curses.aspx IDs already covered by the Curses run, and the rendered bodies are byte-identical. Parsing it would emit 15 duplicate documents sharing an aonid and name with their Curses counterparts.

The source shape is close enough to hazards to reuse that parser's structure directly: a level badge in the title ('Curse 8', 'Disease 0'), trait spans, a Source line, then bold-labelled fields. The stage machinery already exists in universal/ability.py, which detects afflictions from Stage N plus Saving Throw / Onset / Maximum Duration.
design:
Model on pfsrd2/hazard.py, which handles the same shapes. Reuse: restructure pass for the level badge, is_trait for the rarity classes, extract_source_from_bs, extract_bold_fields, universal_handle_save_dc for the Saving Throw, and the existing affliction_stage shape from universal/ability.py.

Field labels observed across both types: Source 118, Saving Throw 102, Effect 59, Stage 1-7 (50/50/50/38/25/12/3), Onset 35, Usage 15 (curses only), Tempted Curse 8, Special 2.
acceptance_criteria: Curses and Diseases parse clean; stages carry structured onset/DC where published; the shared schema reuses creature definitions where the shapes match; ItemCurses is not parsed and the reason is recorded.
close_reason: Affliction parser merged in PFSRD2-Parser#162. 74 curses + 44 diseases, 0 errors. Review also fixed a legacy-edition bug affecting 394 already-shipped hazard files.

title: Item activation: an activatable item grants an action
description:
Nothing in the corpus structures activation. Zero of 141 property rune documents carry an activate or activation field, and 17 of them describe one in prose. The same gap applies to every activatable item — wands, staves, worn items — not just runes, so this does not belong inside the rune-effects work.

Activation is generally an action. That is the modelling insight: an activatable item GRANTS AN ACTION, and the corpus already has a shape for an action — the ability object with an action_type, which creatures and now hazards both use, carrying name, action_type, frequency, requirement, trigger and effect.

So this is not a new vocabulary. It is recognising that 'Activate [one-action] Interact' is an ability the item confers, and extracting it into the shape everything else already uses.

Examples: Glamered ('can be disguised with a mere thought'), Portable ('collapse into a disguised, portable form'), Invisibility, Gliding, Animated, Dancing, Bolka's Blessing ('once per day, the filigree symbol can be activated').
design:
Extract into stat_block.activations as ability objects — same definition creature abilities use, so consumers reuse whatever renders those. The activation cost maps onto action_type; 'once per day' maps onto frequency, which the ability shape already has.

Start with the runes since they are a bounded 17 and the prose is short, then widen to wands and worn items. Do not attempt items whose activation is conditional narrative rather than an action.
acceptance_criteria: An activatable rune carries its activation as an ability with an action_type; frequency limits are structured; items whose activation is not an action keep prose and get needs_review; the shape is identical to the creature ability definition so no new consumer code is needed.

title: Weapon facts on specific magic weapons and precious-material weapons
description:
277 weapon-ish items carry no offense.weapon_modes at all, so nothing about how they hit can be queried:

  Specific Magic Weapons     241  no weapon_modes
  Precious Material Weapons   23  no weapon_modes
  Weapons (misc)              11  no weapon_modes
  Basic Magic Weapons          2  no weapon_modes
  Base Weapons               509  HAVE weapon_modes

This blocks rune eligibility for every one of them: the eligibility clauses key on $.stat_block.offense.weapon_modes[*].weapon_type and [*].damage[*].damage_type, which simply do not exist on these documents. It equally blocks any damage computation, including the tier-1 rune effects.

A specific magic weapon is a composite by nature — Dragon's Tongue is a base weapon plus fixed magic — so this overlaps PFSRD2-Parser-j1w3: either the item carries its own weapon facts, or it carries a composite reference to the base weapon it is built on. Decide which before implementing; carrying both invites them to disagree.
acceptance_criteria: Specific magic weapons can answer weapon_type and damage_type, either directly or through a resolved base-weapon reference; rune eligibility returns a real answer for them; the mechanism agrees with whatever j1w3 lands on.

title: Tier 2: conditional effects — creature-type gates, crit gates, and crafter choice
description:
The vocabulary gap that three separate rune families all hit. Solving them separately would produce three ad-hoc mechanisms.

CREATURE-TYPE GATED (6 documents): Bane, Giant-Killing, Bloodbane, Holy, Anarchic, Axiomatic. 'deals an additional 1d6 mental damage on a successful Strike AGAINST A GIANT'. Bane compounds it: 'the crafter chooses the creature type'.

CRIT GATED: the crit riders on the tier-1 runes and others. Two sub-shapes, both already present in creature data:
- persistent damage — attack_damage with persistent:true ships 564 times on creatures, and one entry ships persistent + notes together
- a damage entry whose note IS the condition: {formula '1d6', damage_type 'fire', notes 'on a critical hit'} ships today
- condition riders ship as modifier entries with prose names and a Conditions link ('sickened 2 and drained 2 on a critical failure', 11 in the offense subtree)

CRAFTER CHOICE (3 armor documents): Energy-Resistant and Energy-Absorbing grant 'resistance 5 to acid, cold, electricity, or fire — the crafter chooses'. The engine already has a 'select' operation for exactly this, currently unused by any shipped effect.
acceptance_criteria: Bane and Giant-Killing carry a target-gated damage effect; the tier-1 runes carry their persistent crit damage using the existing shape; Energy-Resistant uses select; nothing gains a fabricated DC.

title: Tier 1: on-hit damage effects for the 18 unconditional property runes
description:
The narrow, no-schema-change slice of property rune effects. 18 rune documents (~10 runes across two editions) publish an unconditional 'deals an additional NdN <type> damage on a successful Strike':

Astral +1d6 spirit, Brilliant +1d4 fire, Corrosive +1d6 acid, Decaying +1d4 void, Disrupting +1d6 positive, Flaming +1d6 fire, Frost +1d6 cold, Impactful +1d6 force, Nightmare +1d6 mental, Shock +1d6 electricity, Thundering +1d6 sonic, Unholy +1d6 evil.

(Note the remastered name is Shock, not Shocking.)

The text is regular enough for a confident regex, and every damage type needed is already proven in the corpus: spirit 220 entries, evil 204, good 66, holy 1.

No new schema: the effect appends an attack_damage entry, which is the shape creature strikes already use.
design:
effect: { operation: 'add_item', target: '$.stat_block.offense.weapon_modes[*].damage', value: { type: 'stat_block_section', subtype: 'attack_damage', damage_type: 'electricity', formula: '1d6', dice_count: 1, die_size: 6 } }

Two things to confirm on the engine side before committing to add_item:
- PFSRD2-Parser-6xn9 documents that add_item against a strike sub-array skips elements lacking the key. A weapon mode with no damage array would be skipped the same way.
- add_item is currently unused for damage; all 46 shipped effects use replace, add_modifier or adjustment only.

Per-variant, not per-document: Greater grades do not uniformly change on-hit damage. Greater Flaming raises only the persistent crit damage; Greater Giant-Killing raises the on-hit die. Hash over rune name + variant name + variant text as PFSRD2-Parser-14ie specifies.
acceptance_criteria: The 18 documents carry an add_item damage effect per variant that warrants one; applying a shock rune to a longsword yields a second damage entry of 1d6 electricity; no rune outside the 18 gains an effect; greater grades that do not change on-hit damage do not get one.

title: Creature ability enrichment picks a different variant in a full run than a single-file run
description:
Six monster files (slurk x2, rhinoceros x2, kareq x2) come out differently depending on run scope. Parsed alone, Monsters.aspx.ID_788 matches committed data byte for byte under both main and a feature branch. Parsed as part of a full 3,644-file run, the same file loses the 'damage' and 'saving_throw' blocks on its Trample ability.

The parser emits 'WARNING: _pick_best_ability: no edition match for Trample (target=legacy), using first of 2' — the monster-ability lookup finds two Trample variants and picks the first, and which one that is appears to depend on state accumulated during the run.

Found while gating the universal/attack.py hoist: main and branch produced identical output, which is what proved the drift is not change-caused. Related to PFSRD2-Parser-8sgb, which is the equipment equivalent.
design: Make _pick_best_ability deterministic when no edition matches — order the candidates explicitly (by aonid, or by edition then aonid) rather than taking whichever the query returns first.
acceptance_criteria: A full creature run and a single-file run of the same file produce identical JSON; the six files stop drifting; a test covers the two-variant no-edition-match case.

title: Model hazard Melee/Ranged lines as structured attacks
description: Hazards publish attack lines as 'Melee [one-action] scythe +25 [+20/+15] (magical)' followed by 'Damage ...'. The hazard parser currently treats these as abilities named 'Melee' (79) and 'Ranged' (50). No data is lost — action type, traits and structured damage are all captured — but the attack is not modelled as an attack the way creatures do it via parse_attack_action (pfsrd2/creatures.py), which sets offensive_action_type='attack' and parses the attack bonus and MAP progression. Raised by strategic-fragility-reviewer on PR #154. Deferred from that PR because it is new feature scope (attack modelling plus schema additions), not a defect: the published content is all present.
design: Hoist parse_attack_action out of pfsrd2/creatures.py into universal/, then have hazard's ability post-processing route abilities named Melee/Ranged through it. Schema needs the attack fields creature.schema.json already defines.
acceptance_criteria: Hazard Melee/Ranged entries carry a parsed attack bonus and MAP progression; creature output is unchanged; hazards still parse 606/606.
close_reason: Merged in PFSRD2-Parser#157; data in PFSRD2-Data#6.

title: Hazard parser
description:
Parse the 594 Hazards and 13 WeatherHazards pages into structured JSON, modelled as closely as possible on the existing parsers and reusing their code.

Hazards are creature-shaped stat blocks: a level badge (Hazard N), traits, and bold-labelled fields (Complexity, Stealth, Description, Disable, AC, Fort/Ref/Will, Hardness, HP, BT, Immunities, Weaknesses, Resistances, Speed, Routine, Reset), plus abilities carrying action types and Trigger/Effect (Pitfall [reaction] Trigger ... Effect ...).

Label survey across all 594 pages: 842 distinct bold labels, splitting into a closed set of structural field labels and the rest being ability names in bold. Component variants exist ('Trapdoor Hardness', 'Scythe Blade HP', 'HP (per mannequin)') for hazards whose named parts have their own durability.
design:
Reuse rather than reimplement:
  pipeline shape        pfsrd2/feat.py (level badge + traits + bold fields is the closest existing shape)
  bold label extraction universal.universal.extract_bold_fields
  abilities             universal.ability.parse_abilities_from_nodes / parse_ability_from_html
  defenses              universal.creatures universal_handle_immunities / _weaknesses / _resistances / _save_dc
  boilerplate           parse_universal, entity_pass, aon_pass, source_pass, game_id_pass, restructure_pass, edition_pass, remove_empty_sections_pass, trait_db_pass, license_pass, markdown_pass, remove_empty_fields, validate_against_schema
  bin scripts           pf2_hazard_parse / pf2_run_hazards.sh following docs/adding-new-parser.md and the existing bin patterns

Brittle by design: the structural label set is closed and anything outside it is treated as an ability name; an unrecognised construct fails the parse rather than being dropped.
acceptance_criteria: All 594 hazard pages and 13 weather hazard pages parse with 0 errors; output validates against a new hazard.schema.json; abilities carry action_type/trigger/effect; unit tests cover the label extraction, the ability split and the component-durability variants.
close_reason: Hazard parser merged in PR #154. 606/606 hazards and weather hazards parse clean; data merged in PFSRD2-Data#5. Five review rounds, ~125 findings. Follow-ups: PFSRD2-Parser-3t8p (Melee/Ranged as attacks), PFSRD2-Parser-ciet (stealth/saving_throw), PFSRD2-Parser-2lpx (random tables).

title: Spell name corrupted: 'Inner Radiance Torrent to 2 rounds'
description:
spells/secrets_of_magic/inner_radiance_torrent_to_2_rounds.json (aonid 934) has name 'Inner Radiance Torrent to 2 rounds'. The spell is 'Inner Radiance Torrent'; the trailing 'to 2 rounds' is heightening text captured into the name, which also corrupted the generated filename.

Found by bin/pf2_verify_spell_slots: the Celestial Staff lists 'inner radiance torrent' and the reference failed to resolve against the spell corpus. The item side is correct — the spell side is wrong.

This is a spell parser defect, not an equipment one. Worth checking whether other spells with heightened-duration text share the pattern.
design: Inspect the title extraction in pfsrd2/spell.py against Spells.aspx.ID_934.html; the heightening clause is likely adjacent to the title element and being swept into it. Sweep the rest of the spell corpus for names containing ' to ' followed by a duration.
acceptance_criteria: The spell is named 'Inner Radiance Torrent' with a matching filename; pf2_verify_spell_slots resolves the Celestial Staff reference; no other spell name carries heightening text.
close_reason: Fixed. AoN writes a variable cast time into three Secrets of Magic spell titles as 'Name [two-actions] to 2 rounds', and an unbalanced in that markup pushes the name, the action span and the range out of the h1 into #main as loose siblings — so the h1-scoped title cleanup never saw the range and it was concatenated onto the name and the filename. _strip_cast_range_from_title now walks the title region after the h1 and drops a connector-led string following an action span, scoped to stop at the first trait or heading so body action spans are untouched. Inner Radiance Torrent, Horizon Thunder Sphere and Elemental Annihilation Wave all corrected; the three corrupted files were deleted. Full spell run: 0 errors, and the only churn across 2,370 spells is those three renames.

title: Spell slot system: scrolls, wands and staves
description:
Scrolls, wands and staves hold spells, and the slot rules are prose. Decorate them the way runes (q7pm) and materials (xyam) were.

THE INVERSION vs prior slot work: runes and materials decorate an item that exists independently. A scroll or wand is a TEMPLATE until a spell fills it — its level, Price, rarity and traits are all derived from the slotted spell (GM Core 262, 282). The constraint also lives on the spell side, not the host.

Scope: staves (90), wands (60), scrolls (2 generic templates). Grimoires (34 of 36) and spellhearts (32 of 32) carry no rank list and are NOT rank-slot items — out of scope.

Where the data already is:
  - scroll/wand rank tables are already structured in variants; 253 of 273 variants name their rank. 20 do not and need handling.
  - spell identities already resolve via links (game-obj: Spells, aonid).
  - staff spell lists live in THREE places: variants[].text (64), statistics.abilities[].effect (23), stat_block.text (2), in TWO formats: markdown bullets (61) and undelimited run-on strings (26, e.g. Staff of the Black Desert). Whispering Staff correctly has none — it delegates to another staff.
  - wand craft_requirements come in three shapes: fixed spell, open slot, and predicate (casting time, duration, area).

Rules to encode: scroll ranks 1-10, wand ranks 1-9 and NO cantrips/focus spells/rituals (GM Core 282). Staff charges equal the preparer's highest spell rank, casting costs charges equal to the spell's rank, cantrips cost nothing. Those charge rules are universal constants — document, do not store per item.
design:
stat_block.spell_slots on holder items. Scroll/wand templates: capacity 1, allowed_ranks, excluded_spell_types, plus either a fixed spell link or the constraint prose; each variant gains spell_rank so consumers map rank to published level and Price. Staves: entries of {rank, spells[]} parsed out of prose, higher grades ADDING ranks cumulatively.

Cross-links to shipped work: a wand has the Hardness/BT/HP of a thin item of its material (material.statistics keyed by form 'thin'); staves take fundamental but not property runes, which the rune model expresses as capacity but not as a per-item prohibition.
acceptance_criteria: All 90 staves expose structured rank->spells entries regardless of source location or format; scroll and wand variants expose spell_rank; wand slots record the rank ceiling and the cantrip/focus/ritual exclusion; a verifier confirms every referenced spell resolves and every parsed rank is legal for its holder; equipment parser 0 errors; unit tests per location and per format.

title: Property rune effects via the change_records enrichment sidecar
description: The 124 property runes ship with stat_block.rune (slot, requires, conflicts) but no effects — only the 22 fundamental/reinforcing grades have them, hand-authored. Extract property rune mechanics (flat damage adds, resistances, condition-on-crit) the way template changes are enriched: source_type 'equipment_rune' in change_records, hashed over rune name + variant name + variant text so errata to one grade stales only that grade. Never fabricate an effect — a rune whose text does not yield a confident extraction keeps its prose and gets needs_review. This also retrofits staleness detection onto the hand-authored fundamentals, whose static table currently cannot notice errata that changes a number inside an existing rune.
acceptance_criteria: Property runes with extractable mechanics carry effects; the rest carry needs_review; fundamental rune effects move behind the same hashing so errata is detected.
notes:
Rescoped 2026-08-15 after a full survey of the 141 property runes. This ticket is now the DELIVERY MECHANISM — the change_records sidecar, hashing over rune name + variant name + variant text, and the needs_review discipline — while what gets extracted is split by tractability:

  vqjp  tier 1, 18 unconditional on-hit damage runes, no schema change
  ec7r  tier 2, conditional effects, needs a condition qualifier and the unused select operation
  bstt  activation, which is not an effect at all

The original framing ('extract property rune mechanics') understated how heterogeneous the 141 are: only 18 have an unconditional numeric effect, ~50 weapon and ~33 armor runes have no mechanical content at all, and 43 armor runes are a different problem from the weapon ones. The retrofit of staleness detection onto the hand-authored fundamentals still belongs here.

title: Material slot system: structured material metadata, grades, stats table, trait propagation
description:
Materials carry their rules as prose plus a markdown table blob. Decorate them the way runes were decorated (PFSRD2-Parser-q7pm).

Tier 1 (24 Materials items): stat_block.material with precious flag, available grades derived from Object (X-Grade) variants, grade->max item/rune level caps, grants_traits (material traits minus precious), and the Hardness/HP/BT table extracted out of markdown into structured rows keyed by form (thin/item/structure) x grade.

Tier 2 (68 Precious Material Armor/Shields/Weapons use pages): per-variant material_use with grade, form (the shield/buckler split), and the Hardness/HP/BT override stated in variant text.

Key rules: an item takes at most ONE precious material (single slot, not a capacity). Grade exists only when the material is precious - Stone and Bone are in the Materials category, are not precious, and Stone even has a variant literally named 'Stone Object (Low-Grade)', so the precious trait must be the gate, never the variant naming. Grade caps rune level (low 8, standard 15, high unbounded), which is the cross-constraint with the rune slot system.
design:
Trait propagation is verifiable, not asserted: the 68 use pages are AoN's own published answer for every material x item-kind combination, so QA checks derived grants_traits against them. Rarity cannot be a union - 300 base items already carry a rarity trait - so rarity composes as max over common<uncommon<rare<unique while other traits union. The max rule is NOT covered by the oracle (use pages are generic, no base item), so it gets unit tests instead.

Table layouts vary five ways: bold section headers, headers carrying column labels, non-bold headers, no-grade rows (non-precious), and legacy Dragonhide whose table is Dragon Type->Resistance rather than hardness at all. Parser normalizes labels (Standard Items == Items, Structure == Structures) and emits nothing for a table with no recognizable form labels.
acceptance_criteria: All 24 materials get stat_block.material; statistics rows extracted for every material with a hardness table; grants_traits matches all 68 published use pages exactly; shield variants split into grade+form; equipment parser 0 errors; unit tests for each table layout and for rarity max.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: rune and material slot decoration shipped, 0 parser errors, verifiers clean, 49 tests. Follow-on extraction work tracked separately.

title: Equipment parser output is non-deterministic for items sharing an output filename
description:
Two AoN IDs can produce the same output path (e.g. equipment/gm_core/antidote.json from aonid 2879 and 3296; also earplugs, dragon_pearl, travelers_chair, basic_chair, bioluminescence_bomb). Last writer wins, and which one wins varies between runs of the same code.

Measured: three consecutive full equipment runs with no code change between runs 2 and 3 produced different sets of modified files (236 vs 266), with files entering and leaving the diff. The diffs flip aonid, game-id, alternate_link, and source ordering between two published variants of the same item.

Effect: every full equipment run produces ~100 files of phantom churn unrelated to whatever changed, which buries real diffs during review.

Suspect per-process hash randomization (each file is a separate pf2_equipment_parse invocation) reaching a set/dict where ordering decides which variant wins. Worth confirming with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 across two runs before digging further.
design: Two candidate fixes: (a) make the winner deterministic (sort wherever the collision is resolved), or (b) stop colliding — disambiguate output filenames when two aonids map to the same name+source. (b) is the real fix if both variants are legitimately distinct items; (a) is enough if one is meant to supersede the other.
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive full equipment runs with no code change produce zero modified files.

title: Rune slot system: structured rune metadata + fundamental rune effects
description:
Equipment items under item_category='Runes' (129 files, 7 subcategories) carry their slot rules only as prose: statistics.usage.text for eligibility and variants[].text for grade effects. Add structured decoration so consumers can compute which runes fit an item and what they do.

Phase 1 (this issue): stat_block.rune block (form/slot/host/requires/conflicts_with/usage_text) on all rune items, parsed deterministically from item_subcategory + usage text; hand-authored effects for the 12 fundamental/reinforcing variants; grants_property_slots on potency variants.

Phase 2 (separate): regex/LLM extraction of effects for the 124 property runes via the change_records enrichment sidecar (source_type='equipment_rune'), which brings text-hash staleness detection.

Design decisions: capacity, specific-item zero-slot, item level and invested trait are all DERIVED by consumers, not stored per item. Reuses the template effect definition (operation/target JSONPath) rather than a new rune DSL.
design: No new enrichment DB table or version bump in phase 1: fundamental rune effects are hand-authored (12 variants) and requires-parsing is a pure function of the usage string, so there is no uncertain extraction for the hash-keyed sidecar to track. Ceiling: errata changing numbers inside an existing fundamental rune will not be detected. Mitigated by a brittleness assert (every fundamental-subcategory rune must have a table entry) and by moving to the sidecar in phase 2.
acceptance_criteria: All 129 rune items get stat_block.rune; 12 fundamental/reinforcing variants get effects; every requires clause matches >=1 real item and every effect target resolves on >=1 real weapon/armor/shield; equipment parser runs 0 errors; unit tests for usage parsing and effect tables.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: rune and material slot decoration shipped, 0 parser errors, verifiers clean, 49 tests. Follow-on extraction work tracked separately.

title: Extract category/subcategory nav data for equipment types
description: Equipment pages on AoN mark the current category (underlined link in nav h1) and optional subcategory (underlined h2). The parser strips this nav via content_filter before parsing, so category data is lost. Extract it before nav stripping for all 6 equipment types (equipment, armor, weapon, shield, siege_weapon, vehicle), add to schemas (no version bump — nothing consumes this data yet), rerun all equipment.
close_reason: Implemented: item_category/item_subcategory extracted from nav for all 6 equipment types, schema updated, full rerun clean (0 errors, 4616 files gained fields)

title: phantom family: phantom touch grant + force damage conversion unencoded

title: Miniature template: encode 0-ft reach reduction for baseline strikes

title: template-fixes deviations: fabricated change blocks (tengu/corrupt/broodpiercer) + junk corrupt skill effect

title: Revulsion ability text mis-categorized as 'traits' change
description: _categorize_change_text in pfsrd2/enrichment/change_extractor.py misclassifies ability description blocks as change_category='traits' when the text happens to contain 'trait' + action verbs. Example: vampire family's Revulsion ability text ('A vampire can't voluntarily come within 10 feet of...') yields bogus add_item effects for links extracted from the ability body (Concentrate, Condition, Revulsion, Action). These are being written into either $.creature_type.creature_types or $.traits — neither is correct; the whole classification is wrong. Affects ~10 vampire-related monster families. title: _build_damage_effects misses spell damage handling for limited-use abilities
description: Elite/Weak templates say 'If the creature has limits on how many times or how often it can use an ability (such as a spellcaster's spells or a dragon's Breath Weapon), increase the damage by 4 instead.' Current _build_damage_effects in pfsrd2/enrichment/change_extractor.py only emits the +4 to $.offense.offensive_actions[*].ability.damage with conditional 'frequency != null' — covers limited-use abilities (e.g., Breath Weapon) but not spells. Spells have no integer damage field; old cached enrichment annotated this via a string add to $.offense.offensive_actions[*].spells.notes ('+4 damage (Elite, limited use)'). Decide: re-emit the .notes annotation, or design a structural way to express 'spells are limited-use, +4 applies'. Discovered via template re-enrichment drift on bestiary/elite.json.

ENRICHMENT_VERSION bumped 17→18 to invalidate stale cache. Verified on bestiary/elite.json and bestiary/weak.json.

title: _build_combat_stat_effects misses $.offense.offensive_actions[*].spells.spell_attack
description: Elite/Weak template text includes 'attack modifiers' which should bump BOTH Strike attack bonuses AND spell attack rolls. The schema defines offensive_actions[*].spells.spell_attack as a populated integer (627 monsters have it). ENRICHMENT_VERSION bumped 17→18 to invalidate stale cache. Verified on bestiary/elite.json and bestiary/weak.json.

title: Add unit tests for monster_family section preservation
description: Test coverage reviewer flagged PR #103 changes: _section_path_filter (new), _build_subtype (rewritten with JSONPath refs), _consolidate_creation_changes (sections no longer removed), _extract_section_abilities (text preservation invariant). No tests/test_monster_family.py exists.

title: Downstream patch generator: update sibling text fields on numeric adjustments
description: When the downstream patch generator applies an adjustment operation to a numeric field (e.g., saving_throw.dc 15→17), it should also find and replace the old value in any sibling text fields so the human-readable text stays in sync with structured data. Example: elite template adjusts lich Steady Spellcasting DC from 15 to 17, but ability.text and saving_throw.text still say 'DC 15'. Replacement rule: regex (?<\!\d)OLD_VALUE(?\!\d) → NEW_VALUE. Only digit boundaries — letters, signs (+/-/–), spaces, punctuation on either side are fine. This catches DC15, DC 15, +15, –15 but won't false-match 153 or 215.

title: Migrate creature spell notes from string array to modifiers
description: The spells.notes field on creature stat blocks is currently a string array. This caused friction when adding spell damage notes for elite/weak/cryptid templates — the add_item operation's item field in monster_template.schema.json was typed as object-only, and we had to widen it to [object, string] to support appending a bare string to notes. If notes were modifiers (array of {type, subtype, name} objects like everywhere else), add_item with an object item would work naturally and the schema wouldn't need the string exception. Migrating notes to modifiers would make the spell data consistent with how modifiers work across the rest of the creature schema.
